prs.title: fix(formatter): keep trailing double spaces on JSDoc lines
prs.author: costajohnt
prs.body:
Prettier keeps a trailing double space on the middle lines of a `/**` comment (prettier/prettier#18594, in the pinned 3.9.6): it is a Markdown hard line break that doc tooling renders (prettier/prettier#6793). We printed every aligned line through `trim()`, so the spaces were dropped:

```tsx
/**
 * JSDoc with new line using double space
 * It's on another line
 */
```

Match Prettier's `printIndentableBlockComment`: in a `/**` comment (not `/***`), a middle line whose source ends with two or more spaces keeps exactly two after its trimmed content. A bare `*` line, a single trailing space, the opening line, and non-JSDoc block comments are trimmed as before. The check is textual rather than `comment.is_jsdoc()` because the parser also tags `/***` as JSDoc and Prettier's test is textual. The printer never trims text at a line end, so writing the two spaces before the next hard line break is enough.

Fixture `js/comments/jsdoc-trailing-double-space.js` mirrors Prettier's `tests/format/js/comments/trailing-spaces` cases plus a plain `/*` block; its output is byte-identical to Prettier 3.9.8. One line added to `js/crlf/block-comment.js` pins the CRLF output. `cargo test -p oxc_formatter`, clippy and fmt are clean; I did not run the `tasks/coverage` idempotency suites locally.

Written with help from an AI assistant (Claude); reviewed and tested by me.

Closes #26854

prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
As is well known, what counts as JSDoc depends on the consumer, no spec.
e.g. Original JSDoc is strictly limited to `/**`, but TypeScript is not.

Since this doesn't break JSDoc 3, it's more convenient for a formatter to take broader.

Closes #17786

prs.title: fix(formatter): keep comments deferred before an assignment operator
prs.author: waltuov
prs.body:
Closes #23665

Since oxfmt 0.69.0 (#26725), this input loses a comment and prints another one twice:

```ts
type myType /* Comment */
= // Comment
"VALUE"
```

```ts
// oxfmt 0.69.0 and 0.70.0
type myType = // Comment
  // Comment
  "VALUE";
```

The left side of an assignment-like leaves some comments before the operator unprinted, so they lead the right-hand side: an own-line comment, or a block comment that ends its line. When a line comment followed the operator, `operator_line_run` printed it first. `FormatTrailingComments` advances the cursor by count, so it claimed the pending comment instead. That comment was lost and the line comment was printed again as a leading comment. The same happens for `const`, assignments, class and object properties, and for `// oxfmt-ignore` after the operator.

Now nothing glues after the operator while comments before it are pending. Everything leads the right-hand side in source order, like the `as`/`satisfies` site already does. The output is back to what 0.68.0 printed, and for type aliases it matches Prettier 3.9.6:

```ts
type myType =
  /* Comment */
  // Comment
  "VALUE";
```

For JS values Prettier moves the line comment past a short value (`const a = /* c */ 1; // d`). That is covered by `DIVERGENCES.md#eol-comment-after-assign-colon`, so I added a short note there and in AGENTS.md.

Tests: new cases in `operator-eol-line-comment.ts` and `assignment-eol-line-comment.js`. They fail on main and pass with this change. The TS cases

feat(transform-react): add `reportDiagnostics` option to expose recoverable React Compiler diagnostics
prs.author: JacktheRanger
prs.body:
closes #26318

## What

Adds an opt-in `reactCompiler.reportDiagnostics` option to `oxc-transform-react`. When `true`, the recoverable diagnostics the React Compiler produced for a successful compile (`CompileResult::Success { diagnostics }`) are appended to `result.errors` alongside code, keeping the category severity the compiler assigned (`Error` for `Suppression`, `Warning` for `IncompatibleLibrary`, ...). `fatal` keeps its meaning and tells whether `code` is usable.

The default is unchanged: recoverable diagnostics stay omitted, matching Babel's default `logger: null` as decided in #26128.

## Why

Since #26128 (0.148.0) there is no way to learn *why* a function was skipped: `errors` is fatal-only, and `panicThreshold` is not a substitute because it aborts at the first diagnostic without producing code. Consumers that need the reasons — a burndown inventory when adopting the compiler, or checking which `eslint-disable` suppressions actually took effect — lost their only channel. Details and a repro are in #26318.

Two concrete downstream effects on 0.148+:

- `@vitejs/plugin-react` added `logDiagnostics` (vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1431) one day after #26128, reading recoverable diagnostics from `result.errors`; with the current binding that option is a no-op. With this PR it only needs to forward `reportDiagnostics: logDiagnostics`.
- `outputMode: 'lint'` / `noEmit` return `errors: []`, so lint mode has no observable output at the Node boundary.

prs.title: fix(oxlint): skip undefined children in CFG walker
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Fixes #27054.

Bodyless declarations such as `declare module "*.css";` omit the `body` property. Skip `undefined` children in the CFG walker, matching the [regular AST walker's nullish check](apps/oxlint/src-js/generated/walk.js#L20-L21), so JS plugins using code path analysis no longer crash.

Adds oxlint end-to-end coverage for `.ts` and `.d.ts` files, checking that the expected code path events fire.

prs.title: fix(oxlint): skip type-aware lint rules in type-check-only mode
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Pass `type_check_only` through to the TSGolint payload and send files with empty rule lists. Previously, type-aware rules still ran after Oxlint skipped the lint pass that collects disable directives, so suppressed lint errors leaked into `--type-check-only` output and triggered an assertion in debug builds.

Regression snapshots cover suppressed and unsuppressed promises, rule overrides, and a real TypeScript error that must still be reported.

Fixes voidzero-dev/vite-plus#2830.
